## What are Bizard Skills? :brain:

**Bizard Skills** is an AI skill package that turns your AI assistant into a biomedical visualization expert. When you load this skill, your AI can:

- **Recommend** the best visualization type for your data and research question
- **Generate** reproducible R / Python / Julia plotting code adapted from Bizard tutorials
- **Search** across 816 curated figure examples using the included gallery data
- **Link** you to the full tutorial for detailed customization

The skill package works with any AI tool that supports custom instructions or knowledge files:

- **ChatGPT / GPT-4**: Load as custom instructions + knowledge file
- **Claude**: Upload as project files
- **GitHub Copilot Chat**: Reference with `#file:SKILL.md`
- **Local LLMs** (Ollama, LM Studio): Load as system prompt context

## Download the Skill Package {#download}

The ZIP contains:

- **`SKILL.md`** — AI skill instructions: teaches your AI assistant how to use Bizard for visualization recommendations and code generation
- **`gallery_data.csv`** — 816 visualization examples with image URLs, tutorial links, descriptions, and categories
- **`gallery_data_zh.csv`** — Chinese version of the gallery data
- **`README.md`** — Installation guide for different AI tools

## Bizard MCP Server {#mcp}

For AI **agents** (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, …) that can call tools directly, Bizard also ships a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) server: **`@openbiox/bizard-mcp`**.

Unlike the static skill package above, the MCP server serves the **live chart lifecycle** — bilingual search across 800+ chart tutorials, runnable code with dependencies and data URLs, structured adaptation guidance, citation metadata, and template-checked contribution — from a snapshot generated by CI from the same sources as this website and `SKILL.md`, so all three never drift.

::: {.callout-note}
**The skill and the MCP server work together.** They are generated by CI from the same sources, and the MCP prompts (`recommend`, `adapt`, `troubleshoot`, `contribute`) implement the same workflow the skill teaches — so they never contradict each other. The skill plays the playbook role (chart-selection logic and gallery data, usable in any AI tool); the MCP server adds live, exact lookups (search hits with tutorial URLs, runnable code, adaptation checklists, citations, contribution submission). An agent that supports both — e.g., Claude Code with the skill installed **and** the server registered — follows the skill's workflow while grounding every answer in MCP tool results.
:::

No local install needed — **any MCP-capable agent** (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Windsurf, VS Code Copilot Chat, …) can connect to the public hosted instance deployed by the Bizard team. Most clients accept a JSON server entry:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bizard": { "type": "http", "url": "http://biotree.top:38123/bizard-mcp/mcp" }
  }
}
```

In Claude Code, one line is enough:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http bizard http://biotree.top:38123/bizard-mcp/mcp
```

Prefer a fully local setup? Install the package instead:

```bash
claude mcp add bizard -- npx @openbiox/bizard-mcp
```

Or run it with any MCP client over stdio (`npx @openbiox/bizard-mcp`) or your own Streamable HTTP instance (`npx @openbiox/bizard-mcp --http`). See the [MCP server docs](#mcp-docs) below for the full tool list, configuration, and privacy notes.

## MCP Server Details {#mcp-docs}

The full documentation for `@openbiox/bizard-mcp` is maintained in the repository and reproduced here for reference.

### Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `bizard_search` | Bilingual weighted search over the chart gallery; adjacent-category suggestions on zero hits |
| `bizard_list_categories` | All 36 chart categories with per-category chart counts (bilingual names where available) |
| `bizard_get_tutorial` | Chart metadata: packages, example-data URLs, available languages, tutorial link |
| `bizard_get_code` | Runnable tutorial code with package list, example-data URLs, and license notice |
| `bizard_adapt_guidance` | Data-shape checks, dependency prep, parameter mapping, failure modes, alternatives |
| `bizard_cite` | Bizard paper + tutorial citation (bibtex/text/json) with CC-BY-NC-4.0 license notice |
| `bizard_contribute_check` | Validate a draft against the contribution template; preview points |
| `bizard_contribute_submit` | Submit as issue/PR via user credentials, or degrade to draft + deep-link |

Prompts: `recommend`, `adapt`, `troubleshoot`, `contribute` — `chartId` arguments autocomplete via `completion/complete`.
Resources: `bizard://catalog`, `bizard://tutorial/{chartId}` (enumerable via `resources/list`), `bizard://llms-txt`.

If charts or code from Bizard end up in your research, please cite the paper above — the `bizard_cite` tool returns ready-to-paste BibTeX/APA-style citations.

### Deployment

One package, two transports:

- **Local (stdio, default)**: `npx @openbiox/bizard-mcp`. Full capability; contribution runs at level 1/2 when local credentials exist.
- **Hosted (Streamable HTTP)**: `npx @openbiox/bizard-mcp --http`. Port via `BIZARD_HTTP_PORT` (default 3000). Anonymous, stateless. Contribution runs at level 3 (no credentials on the server).
- **Public hosted instance**: `claude mcp add --transport http bizard http://biotree.top:38123/bizard-mcp/mcp` — deployed by the Bizard team; no install required and may be faster to reach from mainland China. Same anonymous/stateless/rate-limited behavior, contribution at level 3.

### Contribution credential degradation

`bizard_contribute_submit` probes the environment on every call and states which level it used — never silently failing:

| Level | Condition | Behavior |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| 1 | `gh` CLI installed and logged in | Creates the issue as your GitHub user (PR submission is planned for a future release) |
| 2 | No `gh`, but `GITHUB_TOKEN` set | GitHub API submission, limited by token scope |
| 3 | Neither (typical for hosted) | Returns formatted draft + pre-filled `issues/new?title=&body=` deep-link |

The server itself holds zero credentials. User free text is truncated (single field ≤ 4000 chars) before being assembled into issue bodies.

### Privacy

Usage feedback is local-only, anonymous, and never networked:

- Appended to `~/.cache/bizard-mcp/usage-log.jsonl` as `{ ts, event, chartId, language, queryHash }` — `queryHash` is the first 8 hex chars of the query's SHA-256 (irreversible).
- Set `BIZARD_USAGE_LOG=off` to disable entirely; set it to a path to relocate the log.
- No server-side telemetry, ever.

Source code and development instructions: [openbiox/Bizard · mcp/](https://github.com/openbiox/Bizard/tree/main/mcp).

## Regenerating Skills

`SKILL.md` is **automatically regenerated** when tutorials are updated on the main branch. To regenerate manually:

```bash
# LLM mode (requires API key in environment)
python .github/scripts/generate_skills.py --verbose

# Offline mode (rule-based extraction)
python .github/scripts/generate_skills.py --offline --verbose
```

See the [Skill Generation Specification](https://github.com/openbiox/Bizard/blob/main/skill-spec.md) for the full technical specification.
